title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section II computes S_0 T_{0,I} for card I = 4. This is the set of 'basic points' (vertices) of the Teichmüller groupoid in genus 0 with 4 marked points, the first nontrivial case of the Teichmüller tower in the Esquisse.

Setup (1).
- J is the set of partitions of I of type (2,2). There are exactly 3, and they correspond to the 3 boundary points of M̄_{0,4}.
- Σ = P^1_J is the projective line with the three points of J marked.
- ω = ω(J) is the 2-element set of cyclic orders (orientations) of J.

Group actions. S_I = S_4 acts on Σ through S_4 → S_J ≅ S_3. The kernel is the Klein group V(I) ≅ (Z/2)^2, an F_2-plane. The margin note says this plane is determined by J; its nonzero vectors, or its dual's, correspond to J, so J ≅ P^1(F_2) and S_J ≅ GL_2(F_2).

Orientations as fixed points (2). The alternating subgroup S_J^+ ≅ Z/3 (also the image of A_4) acts on Σ with exactly two fixed points. In the coordinate where J = {0, 1, ∞}, these are e^{±iπ/3}, the equianharmonic points. The three points of J span a canonical real circle Σ_R (the 'equator'). An orientation of that circle, i.e. a cyclic order on J, picks one hemisphere, hence one fixed point. This gives the bijection ω ≅ Σ^{S_J^+} = Σ^{S_I^+}.

Involution fixed points. For α ∈ J, σ_α is the transposition of J fixing α. It has two fixed points on Σ: α itself and α̃ (e.g. for α = ∞ and z ↦ 1−z, α̃ = 1/2). These are the harmonic points −1, 2, 1/2.

(3)–(4). Set Σ* = Σ \ J. Over C there are canonical (cross-ratio) isomorphisms M_{0,I} ≅ Σ*_I and M̂_{0,I} = M̄_{0,4} ≅ Σ_I, equivariant for S_I.

The figure shows the sphere with poles p, p̃ (the two Z/3-fixed points) and an equator through α, β, γ and α̃, β̃. Thus the special points (orbifold points of M_{0,4}/S_4, plus the tangential directions at the cusps) are described canonically and invariantly; these will serve as base points of the groupoid.

The next page makes this linear: Σ_J = P(V(J)) with V(J) = ker(O^J → O), and computes det V(J) ≅ O(1) twisted by the orientation character Z(ω). The goal is to decide whether the tangent/ψ bundle along section i is O(1) ⊗ Z or O(1) ⊗ Z(ω), i.e. to pin down orientation sign twists needed for canonical tangential base points.
errors: No mathematical error seen. Two conventions are left implicit: which hemisphere goes with which orientation (left- vs right-hand rule), and the realness of the equator (the unique circle through the 3 points, canonical over C).
(3) is written ambiguously; it should read Σ*_I = Σ_I \ J.

ideas.what: Canonical identification M̄_{0,4} ≅ P^1 marked by the 3 partitions of type (2,2), with S_4 acting via S_4 → S_3, kernel the Klein group
ideas.modern_name: Cross-ratio / λ-line; boundary of M̄_{0,4} indexed by (2,2)-partitions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of M_{0,4} and the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: The two Z/3-fixed points (equianharmonic points) canonically indexed by the cyclic orders of J via the hemispheres of the real circle through J
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold points of order 3 of M_{0,4}/S_4, labeled by orientations
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; used as base points in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the special points with automorphisms of order 2 and 3, not this exact labeling

ideas.what: Fixed points α̃ of the transpositions σ_α (harmonic points) as additional special points
Ker(S_4 → S_3) as an F_2-plane whose projective line is J (S_3 ≅ GL_2(F_2))
ideas.modern_name: Klein four-group, exceptional isomorphism S_3 ≅ GL_2(F_2)

missed.claim: This is an explicit, choice-free description of the 'basic points' S_0 T_{0,4}. The equianharmonic points are labeled by orientations of J and lie in hemispheres of the canonical real circle. On the next page this leads to an orientation-twisted determinant line (det V(J) ≅ O(1) ⊗ Z(ω)). It is a careful, canonical treatment of sign and orientation torsors for the base points of the Teichmüller groupoid. It is mostly a bookkeeping refinement of known material.
missed.quote: en associant à x ∈ ω le point fixe sous S_J^+ qui est dans l'hémisphère qui correspond à l'orientation de l'équateur Σ_R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical (torsor-level) labeling of base points matters when making GT/Teichmüller-groupoid constructions functorial with no choices. This is a minor point of rigor rather than a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Classical geometry of M_{0,4} (λ-line, Klein group, order-2 and order-3 special points), set up canonically as groundwork for the Teichmüller tower. It is consistent with the Esquisse and later GT literature. The orientation-torsor bookkeeping is a nice but minor detail.
transcription_corrections: (3) likely reads Σ*_I = Σ_I \ J (the crossed-out symbols are deletions, not a superscript α).

Left margin: 'NB S_I opère sur Σ = Σ_I par l'intermédiaire de S_J, via S_I → S_J → 0; Ker S_I → S_J = V(I), l'ensemble ... espace vectoriel de dim 2 sur F_2 déterminé par J; V(I)* ≃ J' (approximately). The kernel is the Klein group, not 'V(I) → S_I'.
Figure labels: the poles are p and p̃ (the Z/3-fixed points); the equator carries α, β and α̃, β̃.
Bottom-left margin: roughly 'on distingue ... p de p̃ ...', distinguishing the two poles by the orientation.
